children: ENI Q3 adjusted net income €2.8B, pro forma adjusted operating income ~€6.0B. Upstream production 1.83M bpd (up 7%). Extraordinary dividend €0.46/sh and 2026 buyback expanded to €3.8B.
ENI plans a €0.46 extraordinary dividend payable Dec 9, ex-dividend Dec 7. Payment depends on excess cash flow tied to Brent > $90/bbl and stronger-than-expected refining margins.
ENI filed a development plan for Junin 5 heavy oil phase 1 in Venezuela and expects a final investment decision by year-end.
ENI linked to Junin 5 project: phase 1 adds 90 MMcf/d domestic gas; phase 2 could enable ~3.4–3.5 Mtpa LNG exports via a floating facility.
ENI extends fuel price cap through year-end: diesel €2.25/l, petrol €1.99/l. Company will monitor and adjust caps based on market moves and supply via its logistics network.
ENI partners with YPF and ADNOC’s XRG on a multi‑billion Argentina gas export project; consortium will finance about 65–70% of capex and lenders show strong interest.
ENI says Italy fuel price cap will cut results by a few hundred million euros per quarter; about 60% of shipping is under long-term contracts.
DZ Bank raised Eni (ENI) fair value to €31 and kept Buy after strong Q3 earnings, a stronger balance sheet, a special dividend and a third buyback boost.
ENI's retail arm Plenitude bought spot power this summer to cover a surge in customer demand amid tough retail market conditions.
